portInfo.description: GNTO’s Visit Greece page frames Hydra as a Saronic island of maritime heritage and cosmopolitan character: 18th-century merchant fleets, mansions that “stand like fortresses,” and a harbour full of yachts and fishing boats. A call rewards a slow harbour day—museum if open, Kamini if mobility and last-tender allow—more than a multi-site dash. Keep this SeaDays slug distinct from other Argosaronic ports.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Port of Hydra (tender harbour) — Akti Navarchou P. Kountouriotou area, Hydra harbour
gettingThere.distanceToCity: From the tender quay the harbourfront itself is the destination. Visit Greece’s mainland driving notes (Athens → Metochi, then ferry/water taxi) describe how overnight visitors arrive, not a cruise-day itinerary. On a ship call, plan only what the tender schedule supports. Editorial transfer notes (not measured): allow buffer for tender queues both ways; once ashore, budget time for cobbles before climbing inland lanes. Confirm last tender with the ship, not with this guide.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Harbour amphitheatre stroll — mansions, cafés and boats without leaving tender range.
Historical Archives–Museum of Hydra (IAMY) — Struggle relics, gallery and archives when open.
Megalo Kamini coastal walk — only with confirmed last-tender and mobility for the path.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Photograph tender number and harbour landmark before climbing. Hydra’s beauty is vertical; lost time is usually steps and queues, not kilometres.
